Application, driver, whatever your terminology is for your microkernel drivers

pcmattman: Exactly this is why currently I've completely disabled IRQs while drivers are running. Or basically while any kernel code is running, with the exception of the idle task.

I still think working IRQs are an important requirement for a proper CDI implementation. Concurrency issues are something we need to solve at some point, after all
In the end I'm going to move driver code into their own kernel threads, though. IRQs wouldn't be a problem then any more.
But I guess many OSes that start using CDI are in an early stage

Right, so providing concurrency constructs may be as simple as a volatile char in their initial implementation
IRQs are usually one of the first thing people get working, after all
Concurrency however is usually one of the last things people think about
Right
I think if we go forward with the suggestion from the mail thread, we're fine
If you define the interface to only allow one driver function per device to be running (and make that an OS-controlled thing), you offload a bit of effort from CDI driver writers

pcmattman: I don't think your interruptible flag does really gain us anything. When would a driver set it and when not?

This "flag" could easily be a mutex or a similar concurrency construct
